item.title: [1/2] 303 - How LLMs Work - the 20 minute explainer — Fragmented - AI Developer Podcast
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-15 — Daily 2: LLM vocabulary from the ground up, then stress-testing Astra
Why it matters: Reset the foundation at the right level. This recent explainer builds a usable mental model from words to tokens, tokens to embeddings, and embeddings to inference, then introduces temperature and sampling. The aim is not to make you an ML engineer; it is to make the vocabulary in later episodes intelligible before we move on to transformers, training, reasoning and agents.
Source: Fragmented - AI Developer Podcast Original publication: 2026-02-02T08:00:00Z

item.title: [2/2] GPT-6 Astra: The System Card, Alignment and What Comes Next — Don't Worry About the Vase Podcast
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-15 — Daily 2: LLM vocabulary from the ground up, then stress-testing Astra
Why it matters: Yesterday you heard Astra from OpenAI president Greg Brockman. Today, Zvi Mowshowitz works through the actual Astra system card and external evaluations, focusing on the gap between strong capability/safety claims and what the evaluations establish. Pay particular attention to critical cyber capability, evaluation awareness, metagaming, alignment claims and reduced chain-of-thought monitorability. This is a critical reading rather than neutral reporting, so treat Zvi's conclusions as an interpretation too; the primary evidence is OpenAI's system card and the cited external evaluations.
Source: Don't Worry About the Vase Podcast Original publication: 2026-09-10T20:56:19Z

item.title: [1/2] LLM Architecture in 2026: What You Need to Know with Sebastian Raschka — Vanishing Gradients
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-14 — Daily 1: Architecture under the hood, then Astra from the builder
Why it matters: Today’s foundation slot goes deeper under the hood. Raschka walks through how modern LLM architecture has evolved beyond a plain transformer: post-training, inference-time scaling, hybrid architectures, attention variants, KV-cache efficiency, reasoning systems and why implementation details matter. It is the right bridge from a basic mental model of LLMs to understanding why current frontier systems behave and cost the way they do.
Source: Vanishing Gradients Original publication: 2026-04-13T02:52:27Z

item.title: [2/2] Greg Brockman on Astra and the Future of OpenAI — TBPN
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-14 — Daily 1: Architecture under the hood, then Astra from the builder
Why it matters: For the current slot, hear the builder’s account rather than a recap. OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses what Astra changes about computer use and agents, what OpenAI learned from Operator, and how the company thinks about AI systems that carry out longer-running tasks. Treat the capability and scientific claims as OpenAI’s own framing, not independent validation; the value here is direct access to the product and research thesis behind the release.
Source: TBPN Original publication: 2026-09-08T21:50:23Z

item.title: [1/3] How LLMs Actually Work — AI Knowhow
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Foundation week: LLM mechanics, reasoning and the compute bottleneck
Why it matters: Begin with the machinery. This is a compact, accessible explanation of next-token prediction, neural networks, attention, training, hallucination and retrieval-augmented generation. The goal is to build enough of a mental model that later discussions of architecture, reasoning and agents have something concrete to attach to.
Source: AI Knowhow Original publication: 2024-12-02T09:46:00Z

item.title: [2/3] AI Trends 2026: OpenClaw Agents, Reasoning LLMs, and More with Sebastian Raschka — The TWIML AI Podcast (formerly This Week in Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence)
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Foundation week: LLM mechanics, reasoning and the compute bottleneck
Why it matters: Now move from the basic transformer-era model to the modern stack. Sebastian Raschka explains why progress has shifted toward post-training, verifiable-reward reinforcement learning, inference-time reasoning and tool use; he also covers mixture-of-experts, attention efficiency, long context and where agentic systems still fail.
Source: The TWIML AI Podcast (formerly This Week in Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence) Original publication: 2026-02-26T23:52:00Z

item.title: [3/3] Memory chip mania isn’t going away, with Dan Kim — The Economics Show
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-10 — Foundation week: LLM mechanics, reasoning and the compute bottleneck
Why it matters: Finish underneath the models. AI compute is not just about NVIDIA GPUs: memory bandwidth and high-bandwidth memory are becoming binding constraints. This recent FT discussion connects the technical bottleneck to supply, pricing, data-centre economics, China, industrial policy and the physical limits behind continued AI scaling.
Source: The Economics Show Original publication: 2026-09-04T04:00:00Z

item.title: [1/4] The rise and fall of agent civilizations — Dwarkesh Podcast
item.description:
Edition: 2026-09-03 — Agents, architecture, compute and assurance
Why it matters: Start here for the capability shift. A compact account of what happened when many coding agents were allowed to operate together, what emergent coordination looked like, where the system failed, and why multi-agent security now deserves to be treated as an engineering problem rather than science fiction.
Source: Dwarkesh Podcast Original publication: 2026-08-31T20:36:53Z
